title: Aim at what cannot move away
outcomes: Names a target that cannot step aside: a backward pawn whose front square the enemy controls, or a pinned piece
Finds the file along which to attack a backward pawn
Says why a pawn kick on a piece that can move away gains little
Says when there is nothing to aim at

steps.text: Aim at what cannot get away. A **backward pawn** whose front square an enemy pawn controls cannot simply step forward, so you can bring more attackers. A piece **pinned** to its king cannot leave the line of the pin. A piece that can move away is a poor target for a pawn kick: it moves, and the pawn that kicked it can never go back.

steps.caption: White to move. Black's e6 pawn is behind f5, and the d4 and f4 pawns control e5, the square in front of it. The e-file has no White pawn on it (half-open for White), so a rook or queen can use it.

line.say: The queen takes the e-file and attacks e6. A pawn pushed to e5 would meet four attackers and two defenders.

claims.statement: The pawn on e6 is Black's only backward pawn.
The e-file is half-open for White.
After Qe1 four White men attack e5.
After Qe1 two Black men defend e5.
After Qe1 the queen attacks e6.
Qe1, Re1 and Qe2 are all within a fraction of a pawn of the engine's best move.

steps.text: A target is fixed only if it cannot step aside and the attack can bring more units than the defence. Before you push a pawn at a piece, ask where the piece goes. If it has a good square, you have spent a move and left squares behind. Chasing is not always wrong: it can gain space or send a piece offside. This is a *rule of thumb*.

steps.title: Fix it, or chase it?
steps.prompt: The first two items are the same position with the same side to move: one asks about a rook move at the backward pawn, the other about a pawn kick at a knight. Predict each. The third position has nothing to aim at.
In the last position, what did you look for first: a pinned piece, a backward pawn, a piece to chase, or something else? Write what you checked, and whether you reached for a kick first.
